mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen each of the last three weeks (-18.9 to -14.7), indicating a steady return to in-person work. This commuting recovery mechanically increases weekday foot traffic near offices, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -18.9 to -14.7 over last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days fails to exceed the last 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend for at least two more weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has climbed from 4.3 to 7.3 over four weeks, suggesting households are front-loading essential and gift shopping ahead of the Christmas holiday. Once this index crosses +7, the same travel occasions increasingly bundle with discretionary retail stops, pushing RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +7 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM sustaining readings above +7, or RETAIL_REC falls while GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have both improved concurrently (WORKPLACES -18.9 to -14.7; TRANSIT -51.4 to -46.3). Their joint recovery signals restored commuting and errand-chaining behavior, compounding to drive a larger increase in RETAIL_REC than either series would produce alone over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved every week over the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than the growth predicted by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone, or RETAIL_REC declines despite joint improvement in both series.

mechanism_narrative: If regional authorities respond to rising Omicron transmission by tightening restrictions, RESIDENTIAL mobility (currently near 4-6 percent above baseline) would rise sharply as a leading indicator of confinement, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the subsequent two weeks as people reduce discretionary outings.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has stayed in a narrow 4-6 percent band through the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising even after RESIDENTIAL jumps by more than 2 points in a week, indicating no restriction-driven retrenchment.

mechanism_narrative: As December deepens and temperatures drop, PARKS mobility is likely to decline further from its already negative range (-14.3 to -19.9), displacing outdoor leisure activity toward indoor shopping centers during the pre-Christmas period, raising RETAIL_REC within the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fluctuated between -14.3 and -19.9 over the snapshot weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and PARKS both decline together within the next week, indicating no substitution effect from outdoor to indoor activity.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has been gradually declining from 6.0 to 4.1 over the snapshot window, suggesting reduced at-home caution. If RESIDENTIAL falls below 4.0, this signals a durable behavioral shift toward greater willingness to travel for discretionary activities, raising RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 4.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 6.0 to 4.1 across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase even after RESIDENTIAL drops below 4.0, or RETAIL_REC falls while RESIDENTIAL continues declining.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has steadily improved from -51.4 to -46.3, approaching a threshold that typically precedes policy normalization signals (e.g., eased capacity limits). Once TRANSIT crosses above -45, this loosening commonly permits a corresponding rise in RETAIL_REC within two weeks as commuting and errand volumes increase together.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -45 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -51.4 to -46.3 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses -45, or declines despite continued TRANSIT improvement.

mechanism_narrative: Cold-weather displacement of outdoor activity (falling PARKS) combined with continuing office reopening (rising WORKPLACES) jointly push people toward combined commute-and-shop trips, producing a short-term one-week spike in RETAIL_REC beyond what either trend alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -19.9 at t-1w while WORKPLACES rose each week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no short-term uptick within one week despite simultaneous PARKS decline and WORKPLACES increase, indicating the interaction effect is absent.
